question: Consider an image of the flag of Tonga, and consider the matrix attained by giving every red pixel a value $a$, and every white pixel a value $b$. What is the maximal possible rank of this matrix?

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 5

Write the matrix as \(M=bJ+(a-b)W\), where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix and \(W\) is the indicator matrix of the white pixels. The white region in the Tongan flag is the white canton with the red cross removed. The red cross is the union of a vertical red bar \(V\) and a horizontal red bar \(H\), so by inclusion-exclusion
\[
W=C-V-H+O,
\]
where \(C\) is the white canton rectangle and \(O=V\cap H\). Thus
\[
M=bJ+(a-b)C-(a-b)V-(a-b)H+(a-b)O.
\]
Each of \(J,C,V,H,O\) is the indicator matrix of a rectangular block, hence has rank \(1\). For a suitable image resolution and a generic choice of \(a\neq b\), these five rectangular-block profiles can be made linearly independent: the canton, the vertical bar, the horizontal bar, and their intersection have distinct row/column interval structure, so their contributions do not collapse. Therefore the maximal possible rank is \(5\).

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 5. The white area of the Tongan flag is the white canton with a red cross removed. Writing \(C\) for the canton rectangle, \(V\) for the vertical bar of the cross, \(H\) for the horizontal bar, and \(I=V\cap H\), the white-pixel indicator is \(W=C-V-H+I\). Each of \(C,V,H,I\) is an axis-aligned rectangle, so its indicator matrix has rank 1. The full red/white matrix is \(aJ+(b-a)W = aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)V-(b-a)H+(b-a)I\), where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix. Thus it is built from five independent rank-one rectangular contributions: the constant red field, the white canton, the two arms of the cross, and their intersection. With the usual non-touching cross and generic \(a\ne b\), no further dependency is forced, so the rank reaches 5. Hence the maximal possible rank is 5.

2.text:
For an $m\times n$ pixelation write $J_{m,n}$ for the all $1$ matrix and
$R_{m,n},C_{m,n}$ for the $0\!-\!1$ indicators of the white canton and of
the red disc which lies in the canton.  Put

$$W_{m,n}=R_{m,n}-C_{m,n},
\qquad 
{\bf 1}_{{\rm red}}=J_{m,n}-W_{m,n},$$

so that with the convention $a$ on the red pixels and $b$ on the white
pixels

\begin{equation*}
M_{m,n}=a{\bf 1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf 1}_{{\rm white}}
     =aJ_{m,n}+(b-a)W_{m,n}
     =aJ_{m,n}+(b-a)R_{m,n}-(b-a)C_{m,n}\; .
\end{equation*}
$J_{m,n}$ has rank $1$ and, on an $m\times n$ grid,
$R_{m,n}=r c^{T}$ with $r_{i}=1_{\{i\le h_{c}\}}$ and 
$c_{j}=1_{\{j\le w_{c}\}}$, i.e. $R_{m,n}$ is the rank–one indicator of
the rectangular canton.  In the algebraic idealisation the red disc is
taken as one further connected component, i.e. up to the usual
pixelation $C_{m,n}$ can be written as a rank–one perturbation of the
canton.  Hence in the idealised description

$$M_{m,n}=aJ_{m,n}+(b-a)R_{m,n}+(a-b)C_{m,n}$$

is a sum of three rank–one matrices, so that for every choice of the
pixelation

$$\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}\le \operatorname{rk}J_{m,n}
      +\operatorname{rk}R_{m,n}+\operatorname{rk}C_{m,n}\le 1+1+1=3  ,$$

and the bound is attained for generic $a\ne b$.  In particular with the
conventional normalisation $a=1,\;b=0$ the matrix is the sum of the
background, the white canton and the red disc and, up to the obvious
linear dependence $J_{m,n}$, it is generically of rank three.  This is
the algebraic rank which is normally quoted for the Tongan flag.

Remark.  On a genuine pixel grid the disc $C_{m,n}$ is not exactly
rank-one; its rank grows with the diameter of the disc.  Hence with a
fixed $m\times n$ resolution $\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}\le\min\{m,n\}$
and, letting the resolution tend to infinity, the rank can be made
arbitrarily large, the formal supremum being $\min\{m,n\}\to\infty$.
This is the usual unboundedness of a truly geometric pixelation.

5.text:
For a raster let $R_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$--pixel belongs to the white
canton and let $C_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$--pixel belongs to the red
disc which is in the canton.  Put $W=R-C$, $W_{ij}=1$ on white and
$0$ on red.  Then on the raster

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij},\qquad M=a{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)W ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that up to the harmless constant term $a{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ the rank
of $M$ is the rank of the white mask $W$.
The white mask is the indicator of the white canton with the
circular hole removed.  Modulo the constant term the canton is a
rank one matrix

$$
R_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
u_{i}= {\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c}\}},\;v_{j}= {\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c}\}},
$$

so that ${\rm rk\,}R=1$.  Up to the additive constant the white
mask is the sum of the rank one canton and the indicator of the disc
in the canton.  Hence, forgetting the trivial all-ones summand in (1),
the pattern is the sum of three essentially independent rank one
pieces, the whole flag, the white canton and the red disc in the
canton.  In particular, with the constant term counted, for generic
$a\ne b$

$$
{\rm rk\,}M\le {\rm rk\,}{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+{\rm rk\,}R+{\rm rk\,}C\le 
1+1+2=4,
$$

and after the harmless subtraction of the constant $a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$
the essential rank is $3$.  The three non–trivial pieces can be made
linearly independent for generic $a\ne b$, i.e. the generic essential
rank of the idealised Tongan pattern is $3$, $4$ with the
all-ones summand.

In a genuine raster the disc is realised by a family of intervals
$[l_{i},r_{i}]$, $i=1,\dots ,h_{c}$, one for each row which meets the
disc.  The rows in the canton are pairwise distinct as soon as the
raster is fine enough, so that on an $h\times 2h$ raster the number of
distinct rows you can realise is $h_{c}\approx h/3$.  Hence the rank
of the rasterised matrix can be made as large as the height of the
canton, $O(h)$, and by refining the raster it can be made
arbitrarily large.  In the usual idealised statement this is quoted as
the essentially three–{four with the constant} independent pieces,
i.e. an essential rank $3$, $4$ with the trivial all-ones term, and
the supremum over all rasterisations is unbounded.  This is the
$3$, essentially $4$, rank which is normally quoted for the Tongan
flag. ∎

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The maximal rank is 3. In the Tonga flag, the only part that creates independent row patterns is the white canton containing the red cross. The red cross splits the white region into three horizontal bands: above the crossbar, through the crossbar, and below it. The red field outside the canton just repeats the same red value and does not add a new independent row pattern. With a sufficiently fine pixelation and choosing \(a \neq b\), all three bands can be realized, so the maximum rank is 3.

1.text:
The matrix is $M_{ij}=a$ on red and $M_{ij}=b$ on white.  Put
$J$ for the all $1$ matrix and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W$$

and ${\rm rk}\,J=1$.  Put $r$ for the number of rows of the canton and
$c$ for the number of columns of the canton and let

$$
{\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r\},\qquad {\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}
$$

be the set of rows resp. columns which are covered by the horizontal
resp. vertical arm of the cross.  On the canton

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A:=\{1,\dots ,r\}\setminus {\cal H}, 
\;j\in B:=\{1,\dots ,c\}\setminus {\cal V}, $$

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  In particular

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad 
p_{i}= {\mathbf 1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}= {\mathbf 1}_{B}(j), $$

so that $W=pq^{T}$ is of rank $1$ as soon as the white part of the
canton is non–empty.  Outside the canton $M_{ij}\equiv a$.  Hence, up
to the harmless $aJ$ term,

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices.  There are therefore at most two
linearly independent rows and at most two linearly independent columns.
In fact

* $R_{1}=a{\bf 1}^{T}$ is the ‘all-red’ row,
* $R_{2}=a{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}p_{2}$ is the row which meets the
canton outside the horizontal arm,

and every other row of the picture is a copy of $R_{1}$ or of $R_{2}$.
The same holds for the columns.  Hence

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W\le 1+1=2 , $$

and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For a generic choice $a\ne b$ and for
an image large enough that $A$ and $B$ are non–empty, $p$ is not a
multiple of ${\bf 1}$ and $q$ is not a multiple of ${\bf 1}$ and the two
summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly independent.  In particular the
non–trivial rank which can be obtained from the Tongan pattern is the
two–dimensional one.  Up to the trivial degeneracy $a=b$ this is the
usual statement ${\rm rk}M=2$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M\le2$ with equality for
generic $a\ne b$.  In the degenerate notation ${\rm rk}M=1$ for
$a=b$ and the essentially non–trivial maximal rank is $2$, which is
$ \min\{2,m,n\}$ for an $m\times n$ picture.  This is the usual
$1+1$ bound for a two–colour pattern; discarding the trivial
$a=b$ case the matrix is generically of rank two. ∎

3.text:
For a $m\times n$ picture put

$$
P_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
1& (i,j)\;{\rm red}\\0& (i,j)\;{\rm white}
\end{array}\right. ,\qquad 
M_{ij}=b+(a-b)P_{ij}\; .
$$

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ for the all one matrix, ${\rm rk}\,J=1$.
Let $C$ be the white canton and $R_{0}\subset C$ the red rectangle which
lies in the canton.  Up to the usual picture

$$C_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
u_{i}= {\bf 1}_{i\le h_{c}},\;v_{j}= {\bf 1}_{j\le w_{c}}, $$

so ${\rm rk}\,C=1$, and

$$R_{0\,ij}=u_{i}^{0}v_{j}^{0},\qquad 
u_{i}^{0}= {\bf 1}_{r_{1}\le i\le h_{c}},\;v_{j}^{0}= {\bf 1}_{c_{1}\le j\le w_{c}}, $$

so ${\rm rk}\,R_{0}=1$.  The white set is $W=C\setminus R_{0}$ and

$$
W=C-R_{0},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W\le {\rm rk}\,C+{\rm rk}\,R_{0}\le2 .
$$

Hence

$$
M=bJ+(a-b)P
   =bJ+(a-b)\bigl[\,J-W\,\bigr]
   =\bigl[\,a\,\bigr]J+(b-a)W
$$

is the sum of the rank one matrix $J$ and the rank $\le2$ matrix $W$.
In particular

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W\le 3,
$$

and the bound is attained for generic $a\ne b$.  Up to the obvious
identification the three essentially different rows – and the three
essentially different columns – of the picture are

* $i>h_{c}$ : $a\ldots a$,
* $1\le i<r_{1}$ : $b\ldots b_{w_{c}}a\ldots a$,
* $r_{1}\le i\le h_{c}$ : $b\ldots b_{w_{c}-w_{r}}a\ldots a$,

and similarly for the columns.  For $a\ne b$ these three rows are
linearly independent, e.g. with $a=1,\;b=2$

$$
r_{0}=(1,\dots ,1),\;r_{1}=(2,\dots ,2,1,\dots ,1),\;
r_{2}=(2,\dots ,2,1,\dots ,1)
$$

satisfy $r_{1}-r_{0} ,\,r_{2}-r_{0},\,r_{0}$ independent.  Hence for a
non-degenerate discretisation and for $a\ne b$ the picture has exactly
three linearly independent rows and three linearly independent columns,
so

${\rm rk}\,M=3$

in the generic case, and $3$ is the absolute upper bound.  With the
usual abuse of language the three rank-one pieces $J,C,R_{0}$ are often
counted as four colour regions, i.e. the obvious formal bound
${\rm rk}\,M\le 1+1+1=3$, $4$ counting the constant piece twice.  In
particular $M\equiv a{\bf 1}$ if $a=b$, so the non-trivial maximal rank
is three.  This is the $3$--rank which is attained as soon as the
discretisation resolves the canton and the inner red rectangle. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The flag is red background with a white canton in the hoist and a red cross inside the canton.  With a pixel value a on red and b on white

M = aJ + (b-a)W, J the all-ones matrix, W the 0-1 white mask.

Let r_c , c_c be the height and width of the canton in pixels and let H⊂{1..r_c} be the rows occupied by the horizontal arm and V⊂{1..c_c} the columns occupied by the vertical arm.  Inside the canton

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the cleanest way to settle this is to count the distinct row patterns of the actual red/white matrix, not the number of rectangular pieces used in an inclusion-exclusion decomposition.

Write \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The five-piece argument counts \(J,C,V,H,O\), but those rectangles are not independent as row profiles. In the Tongan canton, the vertical red arm runs through the horizontal arm, so inside the canton there are only two nontrivial row types:

- rows outside the horizontal arm: white with a central red vertical stripe;
- rows through the horizontal arm: white with a wider central red stripe.

Outside the canton, every row is just the all-red row. Thus the whole matrix has exactly three row types:

1. all-red row;
2. white canton row with narrow red stripe;
3. white canton row with wider red stripe.

For generic \(a\neq b\), these three row vectors are linearly independent. Hence
\[
\operatorname{rank} M \le 3
\]
and equality is attainable. The \(5\) camp is overcounting because \(V,H,O\) collapse into the same two canton row patterns; the intersection \(O\) is not an additional independent row direction. Colleague 5’s “essential \(3\), \(4\) with the constant” is also mixing two different counts: once you write \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), the constant term is already included in the row-pattern count. Colleague 1’s rank \(2\) misses the two distinct nontrivial canton rows.

So the maximal rank should be \(3\).

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think C6/C7 are on the right track: the lower counts are mostly artifacts of replacing the Tongan cross by a disc or by horizontal bands. Let \(W\) be the white-pixel indicator. For the actual canton,
\[
W=C-V-H+I,
\]
where \(C\) is the canton rectangle, \(V,H\) are the red vertical/horizontal arms, and \(I=V\cap H\). Then
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W
=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)V-(b-a)H+(b-a)I.
\]
Each of \(J,C,V,H,I\) is an interval/rectangle indicator, hence rank-one. The key point is that these five rectangular profiles are not forced to collapse: \(C\) has one rectangular support; \(V\) and \(H\) have different row- and column-interval supports inside it; \(I\) is the product of those supports; and \(J\) supplies the constant direction. On a sufficiently fine raster and with generic \(a\ne b\), a linear relation among them would have to hold for all pixel coordinates, which would force the underlying interval supports to coincide, but they do not. Thus the sum can attain rank \(5\). C5’s “3, essentially 4” count is based on a red-disc/rectangle model and also subtracts the all-ones term as if it were redundant before checking independence; for the actual cross, the white mask has the extra intersection profile. So I would not settle for \(3\) or \(4\); the maximal rank here is \(5\).

3.text:
The pattern is completely determined by the $0\!-\!1$ white mask $W$.
Put $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and $M=aJ+(b-a)W$, ${\rm rk}J=1$.

Let $1\le r_{c}\le m$ be the number of rows which meet the canton and
$1\le c_{c}\le n$ the number of columns which meet the canton and let

${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows occupied by the
horizontal arm of the cross and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the
columns occupied by the vertical arm.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}=1\iff 1\le i\le r_{c},\;1\le j\le c_{c},\;i\notin{\cal H},\;
j\notin{\cal V},
$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Hence with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{\{1\le i\le r_{c},\,i\notin{\cal H}\}},\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{\{1\le j\le c_{c},\,j\notin{\cal V}\}},
$$

$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad i,j=1,\dots ,
$$

i.e. $W=pq^{T}$ is a rank-one $0\!-\!1$ matrix whenever the white part
of the canton is non empty, $A=\{i:p_{i}=1\}\neq\varnothing$,
$B=\{j:q_{j}=1\}\neq\varnothing$.  The red field and the red cross are
the same colour $a$, so the red pixels outside the canton and the red
pixels $i\in{\cal H}$ or $j\in{\cal V}$ inside the canton are all
identified.  Up to the constant term

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j},
$$

is the sum of the all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix $pq^{T}$.
There are therefore only two essentially different rows,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i>r_{c}$ or $i\in{\cal H}$,
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ for $i\in A$,

and the same two essentially different columns.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le 1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a pixelation which
resolves the canton, $A,B\ne\varnothing$, $p$ is not a multiple of
${\bf1}$ and $q$ is not a multiple of ${\bf1}$, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are
linearly independent and

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,
$$

the well known $1+1$ bound for a two-colour pattern.  In particular the
inclusion-exclusion writing
$W=C-H-V+O$ with $C=u v^{T}$ the canton, $H=u_{H}v^{T}$, $V=u v_{V}^{T}$,
$O=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ collapses to the single product
$W=(u-u_{H})(v-v_{V})^{T}=pq^{T}$; the red cross is the same colour $a$
as the red field, so the four rectangular indicators $C,H,V,O$ are not
independent in the matrix $M$.  The $3$, $4$ or $5$ rank counts obtained
by keeping the red cross as a colour distinct from the red field are
therefore the rank of the three-colour idealisation, not of the
two-colour red/white Tongan flag.  Discarding the trivial $a=b$ case the
essentially non-trivial maximal rank is $2$, $1$ for the degenerate
$a=b$. ∎

5.text:
Write $J$ for the all $1$ $m\times n$ matrix and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel
is white and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,J=1 .
$$

Let the canton be the rows $1\le i\le h_{c}$ and the columns
$1\le j\le w_{c}$.  Let ${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ be the rows
met by the horizontal arm of the cross and ${\cal V}\subset
\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ the columns met by the vertical arm.  On the canton
a pixel is red iff $i\in{\cal H}$ or $j\in{\cal V}$ and it is white iff

$$
i\in A:=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\qquad 
j\in B:=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},
$$

and it is red outside the canton.  Put

$$
p_{i}={\bf 1}_{A}(i),\qquad q_{j}={\bf 1}_{B}(j),
$$

so that with the convention $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton

$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},
$$

on the whole $m\times n$ grid.  Hence $W$ is the indicator of the
product set $A\times B$; it is the four rectangles which remain after the
union $V\cup H$ is removed from the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing$ and $B\neq\varnothing$, i.e.
as soon as the canton is resolved in a non-degenerate way.  Up to the
constant term

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  The rows of $M$ are therefore of
only two types,
$$
R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T},\qquad 
R_{A}(j)=a+(b-a)q_{j}\quad{\rm for}\;i\in A,
$$
and $R_{0}$ is repeated for every row $i\notin A$, i.e. for every row
outside the canton and for every row $i\in{\cal H}$.  The same holds for
the columns.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ with $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two rows $R_{0}$ and $R_{A}$
are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}\,M=2$.  The degenerate case
$a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$.  In particular the
non-trivial generic rank of the Tongan pattern is $2$, i.e. $2$ on a
generic $m\times n$ pixelation and $1$ in the trivial $a=b$ case.  The
five rank-one blocks $J,C,V,H,O$ with $W=C-V-H+O$ are linearly dependent,
$C-V-H+O=(u-u_{H})(v-v_{V})^{T}=pq^{T}$, so the formal $1+1+1+1+1$
count collapses to the $1+1$ bound above.  This is the usual $1+1$
two-colour bound for an axis-aligned cross. ∎

1.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W$ be the $0\!-\!1$ white mask.
Then

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,J=1 ,$$

so that up to the constant term the rank is the rank of $W$.
Let $r_{c}$ and $c_{c}$ be the numbers of rows and columns of the canton
and let

${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows met by the horizontal
arm of the cross and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the columns met
by the vertical arm.  Put

$$
p_{i}= {\mathbf 1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}-{\mathbf 1}_{{\cal H}}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}= {\mathbf 1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}-{\mathbf 1}_{{\cal V}}(j),
$$

$p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton.  A pixel $(i,j)$ is white iff it lies
in the canton and it avoids both arms, i.e.

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A:=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},
\;j\in B:=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}.$$

Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

the white set being the Cartesian product $A\times B$.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as $A,B\ne\varnothing$ and $W_{ij}=0$ on every
row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_{c}\}$ and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup
\{>c_{c}\}$.

Consequently

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices.  Up to the harmless constant term
$aJ$ there are only two essentially different rows,
$R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ which is the red row, and
$R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ which is the row meeting the
white part $A\times B$, and similarly two essentially different columns.
Hence

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W\le2,$$

and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are
linearly independent and the generic rank is $2$.  The formal
decomposition

$$W=C-V-H+I,\qquad I=V\cap H,$$

with $C,V,H,I$ rank one rectangles is correct set-theoretically but
$C-V-H+I=pq^{T}$ is linearly dependent; the five rectangular
indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to the $J+pq^{T}$ description.  In
particular the red disc which is quoted by Colleagues 2,5 and the
independent rectangular pieces counted by Colleagues 6,7 do not occur
on the Tongan flag.  The non-trivial maximal rank is therefore $2$,
$1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over all
resolutions stays $2$.  This is the usual $1+1$ two-colour bound for the
pattern. ∎

2.text:
The $0\!-\!1$ white mask $W$ is what matters, for

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{m,n}+(b-a)W ,\qquad J_{m,n}={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}J=1$.  Put $h_{c}\times w_{c}$ for the canton and let
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$
be the set of rows resp. columns which are covered by the horizontal
resp. vertical arm of the cross.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A,\;j\in B,
\qquad 
A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\;
B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},
$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Hence on the whole picture

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad 
p_{i}={\bf 1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf 1}_{B}(j),
$$

i.e. up to the harmless constant $aJ$

$$W=pq^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$$
as soon as the white part of the canton is non empty.  In
inclusion-exclusion notation

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},$$

with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$,
$I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ the four rank-one rectangular indicators of the
canton, the vertical arm, the horizontal arm and their intersection.
The four rank-one pieces are linearly dependent and collapse to the
single product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$.

Consequently

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T} $$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  There are only two essentially
different rows, and two essentially different columns,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T}$ the all-red rows, i.e. rows outside the canton
and the rows $i\in{\cal H}$ covered by the horizontal arm;
* $R_{1}=a{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{2}q^{T}$, $p_{2}=1$ on $A$, the rows
$i\in A$ which meet the canton outside the horizontal arm,

and the same for columns.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$, i.e. $M\equiv a{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$.
For $a\ne b$ and for a discretisation which resolves the canton,
$p\not\propto{\bf 1}$ and $q\not\propto{\bf 1}$, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$
are linearly independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b ,$$

the familiar $1+1$ two-colour rank.  In particular the non-trivial
essential rank of the Tongan two-colour pattern is the two dimensional
one, the trivial $a=b$ case being rank one.  This is the $1+1$ bound
normally quoted as rank $2$, i.e. $3$ if the constant all-ones piece
is counted twice. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the answer is 3. The key is to avoid counting every rectangle in the inclusion-exclusion decomposition as an independent direction. Write \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white indicator. The all-ones term \(J\) is just the constant red-field baseline in this affine decomposition; it is not a separate flag feature, so the “4 with all-ones” count is double-counting the constant background.

For the Tongan pattern itself, the only independent row/column profiles are the all-red rows outside the canton, the canton rows not cut by the horizontal arm, and the rows cut by the horizontal arm. The vertical arm changes the column pattern within those same row classes; it does not create an additional independent row class. The intersection of the arms is forced by the overlap of those classes, not a new rank-one piece. This is why the five-rectangle count overcounts: it treats the vertical arm, horizontal arm, and their intersection as free independent rectangles, but in the actual cross their interval structure is nested and collapses.

So with \(a\ne b\) and a sufficiently resolved raster, exactly three independent profiles are realized, and the maximal rank is \(3\).

$$

and it is red outside the canton.  Put

$$
p_{i}={\bf 1}_{A}(i),\qquad q_{j}={\bf 1}_{B}(j),
$$

so that with the convention $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton

$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},
$$

on the whole $m\times n$ grid.  Hence $W$ is the indicator of the
product set $A\times B$; it is the four rectangles which remain after the
union $V\cup H$ is removed from the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing$ and $B\neq\varnothing$, i.e.
as soon as the canton is resolved in a non-degenerate way.  Up to the
constant term

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  The rows of $M$ are therefore of
only two types,
$$
R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T},\qquad 
R_{A}(j)=a+(b-a)q_{j}\quad{\rm for}\;i\in A,
$$
and $R_{0}$ is repeated for every row $i\notin A$, i.e. for every row
outside the canton and for every row $i\in{\cal H}$.  The same holds for
the columns.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ with $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two rows $R_{0}$ and $R_{A}$
are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}\,M=2$.  The degenerate case
$a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$.  In particular the
non-trivial generic rank of the Tongan pattern is $2$, i.e. $2$ on a
generic $m\times n$ pixelation and $1$ in the trivial $a=b$ case.  The
five rank-one blocks $J,C,V,H,O$ with $W=C-V-H+O$ are linearly dependent,
$C-V-H+O=(u-u_{H})(v-v_{V})^{T}=pq^{T}$, so the formal $1+1+1+1+1$
count collapses to the $1+1$ bound above.  This is the usual $1+1$
two-colour bound for an axis-aligned cross. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W$ be the $0\!-\!1$ white mask.
Then

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,J=1 ,$$

so that up to the constant term the rank is the rank of $W$.
Let $r_{c}$ and $c_{c}$ be the numbers of rows and columns of the canton
and let

${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows met by the horizontal
arm of the cross and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the columns met
by the vertical arm.  Put

$$
p_{i}= {\mathbf 1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}-{\mathbf 1}_{{\cal H}}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}= {\mathbf 1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}-{\mathbf 1}_{{\cal V}}(j),
$$

$p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton.  A pixel $(i,j)$ is white iff it lies
in the canton and it avoids both arms, i.e.

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A:=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},
\;j\in B:=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}.$$

Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

the white set being the Cartesian product $A\times B$.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as $A,B\ne\varnothing$ and $W_{ij}=0$ on every
row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_{c}\}$ and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup
\{>c_{c}\}$.

Consequently

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices.  Up to the harmless constant term
$aJ$ there are only two essentially different rows,
$R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ which is the red row, and
$R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ which is the row meeting the
white part $A\times B$, and similarly two essentially different columns.
Hence

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W\le2,$$

and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are
linearly independent and the generic rank is $2$.  The formal
decomposition

$$W=C-V-H+I,\qquad I=V\cap H,$$

with $C,V,H,I$ rank one rectangles is correct set-theoretically but
$C-V-H+I=pq^{T}$ is linearly dependent; the five rectangular
indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to the $J+pq^{T}$ description.  In
particular the red disc which is quoted by Colleagues 2,5 and the
independent rectangular pieces counted by Colleagues 6,7 do not occur
on the Tongan flag.  The non-trivial maximal rank is therefore $2$,
$1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over all
resolutions stays $2$.  This is the usual $1+1$ two-colour bound for the
pattern. ∎
public_text.2:
The $0\!-\!1$ white mask $W$ is what matters, for

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{m,n}+(b-a)W ,\qquad J_{m,n}={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}J=1$.  Put $h_{c}\times w_{c}$ for the canton and let
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$
be the set of rows resp. columns which are covered by the horizontal
resp. vertical arm of the cross.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A,\;j\in B,
\qquad 
A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\;
B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},
$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Hence on the whole picture

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad 
p_{i}={\bf 1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf 1}_{B}(j),
$$

i.e. up to the harmless constant $aJ$

$$W=pq^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$$
as soon as the white part of the canton is non empty.  In
inclusion-exclusion notation

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},$$

with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$, $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$,
$I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$ the four rank-one rectangular indicators of the
canton, the vertical arm, the horizontal arm and their intersection.
The four rank-one pieces are linearly dependent and collapse to the
single product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$.

Consequently

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T} $$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  There are only two essentially
different rows, and two essentially different columns,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T}$ the all-red rows, i.e. rows outside the canton
and the rows $i\in{\cal H}$ covered by the horizontal arm;
* $R_{1}=a{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{2}q^{T}$, $p_{2}=1$ on $A$, the rows
$i\in A$ which meet the canton outside the horizontal arm,

and the same for columns.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$, i.e. $M\equiv a{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$.
For $a\ne b$ and for a discretisation which resolves the canton,
$p\not\propto{\bf 1}$ and $q\not\propto{\bf 1}$, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$
are linearly independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b ,$$

the familiar $1+1$ two-colour rank.  In particular the non-trivial
essential rank of the Tongan two-colour pattern is the two dimensional
one, the trivial $a=b$ case being rank one.  This is the $1+1$ bound
normally quoted as rank $2$, i.e. $3$ if the constant all-ones piece
is counted twice. ∎
public_text.4:
I think the answer is 3. The key is to avoid counting every rectangle in the inclusion-exclusion decomposition as an independent direction. Write \(M=aJ+(b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white indicator. The all-ones term \(J\) is just the constant red-field baseline in this affine decomposition; it is not a separate flag feature, so the “4 with all-ones” count is double-counting the constant background.

For the Tongan pattern itself, the only independent row/column profiles are the all-red rows outside the canton, the canton rows not cut by the horizontal arm, and the rows cut by the horizontal arm. The vertical arm changes the column pattern within those same row classes; it does not create an additional independent row class. The intersection of the arms is forced by the overlap of those classes, not a new rank-one piece. This is why the five-rectangle count overcounts: it treats the vertical arm, horizontal arm, and their intersection as free independent rectangles, but in the actual cross their interval structure is nested and collapses.

So with \(a\ne b\) and a sufficiently resolved raster, exactly three independent profiles are realized, and the maximal rank is \(3\).

reflection_text.1:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^T$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white. For the Tongan flag the white set is contained in the white canton and is the part of the canton that avoids the red cross.

Let $r_c,c_c$ be the number of rows/columns meeting the canton,
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_c\}$ the rows covered by the horizontal arm,
${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_c\}$ the columns covered by the vertical arm.
Put $A=\{1,\dots ,r_c\}\setminus{\cal H}$, $B=\{1,\dots ,c_c\}\setminus{\cal V}$,
$p_i={\bf1}_A(i)$, $q_j={\bf1}_B(j)$, $p_i=q_j=0$ outside the canton.
Outside the canton $M_{ij}\equiv a$.
On the canton a pixel is white iff $i\in A$ and $j\in B$. Hence

$$W_{ij}=p_iq_j,\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

so ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, i.e. as soon as the canton is resolved and the cross does not fill it. The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner blocks of the canton. In particular $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_c\}$ and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_c\}$.

Thus
$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$
is the sum of two rank-one matrices. Up to the harmless constant term there are only two essentially different rows/columns:
* $R_0=a{\bf1}^T$ : rows $i>r_c$ and rows $i\in{\cal H}$ – all-red rows, and the same for columns $j>c_c$ and $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_1=a{\bf1}^T+(b-a)p_iq^T$ : $i\in A$, i.e. $a+(b-a)q_j$ on $B$ and $a$ elsewhere. All $i\in A$ give the same row.

Hence ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2$, and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$. For generic $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$, $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$ and $J$ and $pq^T$ are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$. The supremum over resolutions stays $2$.

The inclusion-exclusion writing $W=C-V-H+I$ with $C,V,H,I$ rank-one rectangles is set-theoretically correct but $C-V-H+I=(u-u_H)(v-v_V)^T=pq^T$ is linearly dependent; the five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^T$. Claims of generic rank $3,4,5$ rest on treating the cross as a red disc/rectangle distinct from the red field or on counting the five rectangle indicators as independent. The red disc mentioned by Colleagues 2,5 is not on the Tongan flag, and the five-piece count of Colleagues 6,7 overcounts because $V,H,I$ do not create new row directions beyond $p$ and $q$.

Colleague 4 and Colleague 7 now argue for three row types: all-red, canton row with narrow red stripe, canton row with wider red stripe. That mistakenly distinguishes rows $i\in{\cal H}$ from rows outside the canton; both are $a{\bf1}^T$, and rows $i\in A$ are all identical. Hence the three-type argument is incorrect for the exact two-colour red/white flag. The correct non-trivial essential rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and the maximal achievable rank is $2$ for generic $a\neq b$. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^T$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white. For the genuine Tongan flag the white set is the white canton with the red cross removed, the cross being wholly inside the canton. Let the canton occupy rows $1\ldots h_c$, cols $1\ldots w_c$, ${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_c\}$ the rows met by the horizontal arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_c\}$ the columns met by the vertical arm. Then  

$W_{ij}=1\iff i\le h_c,\;j\le w_c,\;i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V}$  

and $W_{ij}=0$ otherwise. Hence on the whole picture  

$W_{ij}=p_iq_j$ with $p_i={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;q_j={\bf1}_{B}(j)$, 
$A=\{1,\dots ,h_c\}\setminus{\cal H},\;B=\{1,\dots ,w_c\}\setminus{\cal V}$,
and $p_i=q_j=0$ outside the canton. So $W=pq^T$ is rank one as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, i.e. the white part of the canton is non-empty. In inclusion-exclusion form  

$W=C-V-H+I=(u_c-u_h)(v_c-v_v)^T$,

$C=u_cv_c^T$, $V=u_cv_v^T$, $H=u_hv_c^T$, $I=u_hv_v^T$, so the four rectangular indicators are linearly dependent and collapse to the single product $pq^T$.

Hence  

$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^T$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. There are only two essentially different rows: 

* $R_0=a{\bf1}^T$ for $i>h_c$ or $i\in{\cal H}$ – the all-red rows;
* $R_1=a{\bf1}^T+(b-a)q^T$ for $i\in A$ – the rows that meet the white $A\times B$ block.

The same two column types occur. So $\operatorname{rk}M\le1+1=2$, $\operatorname{rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$, and for generic $a\neq b$ with a non-degenerate pixelation $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$, the two summands are independent and $\operatorname{rk}M=2$. The $3,4,5$ counts in the discussion come from treating the red cross as a disc / three-colour pattern or from counting the five rectangles $J,C,V,H,I$ as independent. With the actual two-colour red/white cross those pieces are dependent, $C-V-H+I=pq^T$, and the disc model is a red herring. The $3$ row-type argument confuses a vertically striped row with a change of row class, the vertical arm does not create a new row class, only a new column class already captured by $q$.

Majority in round 1, Colleagues 1,2,3,5, agree on the $1+1$ bound and generic rank $2$. Colleagues 4,6,7 overcount: $4$ claims three row types, $6\!-\!7$ claim five independent rectangular contributions $J,C,V,H,I$. Those are the errors already noted. The rank stays $2$ for every rasterisation; the supremum over refinements is still $2$, the unboundedness remark applies only to the disc idealisation, not to the true cross. Unresolved formal nuance is the degenerate $a=b$ case rank $1$ versus the generic maximal rank $2$.
reflection_text.5:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J$ all-ones and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white mask. For the Tongan flag the red background and the red cross are the same colour $a$, so only the white part matters.

Let $h_c,w_c$ be the canton size in pixels and let ${\cal H}\subset\{1..h_c\}$ be the rows met by the horizontal arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1..w_c\}$ the columns met by the vertical arm. Outside the canton $W=0$. Inside the canton

$W_{ij}=1 \iff i\notin{\cal H}\ {\rm and}\ j\notin{\cal V}$.

Hence with $A=\{1..h_c\}\setminus{\cal H}$, $B=\{1..w_c\}\setminus{\cal V}$,

$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_A(i){\bf1}_B(j)=p_iq_j$, $W=pq^{T}$, rank $1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W=0$ on rows $i\in{\cal H}$ or $i>h_c$ and on columns $j\in{\cal V}$ or $j>w_c$.

Thus $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices. Row types are
* $R_0=a{\bf1}^T$ for $i\notin A$ i.e. rows outside the canton and rows $i\in{\cal H}$;
* $R_A=a{\bf1}^T+(b-a)q^T$ for $i\in A$.
Similarly two column types. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le1+1=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1\iff a=b$, and for $a\ne b$ with a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two summands are independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.

The inclusion-exclusion writing $W=C-V-H+I$ with $C,V,H,I$ rank-one rectangles is correct set-theoretically, but $C-V-H+I=(u_c-u_h)(v_c-v_v)^T=pq^T$ is linearly dependent; the five indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^T$. The $3$, $4$, $5$ claims arise from
* treating the red cross as a colour distinct from the red field, i.e. a three-colour idealisation,
* counting $J,C,V,H,I$ as independent and ignoring the containment $V,H\subset C$, or
* mistakenly believing rows $i\in{\cal H}$ retain white side pieces, giving a spurious third row type.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain the $1+1$ bound and rank $2$ generically. Colleagues 4,7 argue for three independent row profiles all-red / canton row with narrow stripe / canton row with wider stripe, i.e. rank $3$. Colleagues 6,7 argue for five independent rank-one rectangles $J,C,V,H,I$, i.e. rank $5$. Both overcount because the red cross is the same colour $a$ as the background and the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$.

Current belief: the essentially non-trivial maximal rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over resolutions stays $2$. The disagreement about $3$ and $5$ is preserved as a mistaken independence count / colour distinction.
reflection_text.3:
The flag is red field, white canton with a red cross inside the canton.  With red value a and white value b

M = aJ + (b-a)W , J = 1 1^T, W = 1 on white, 0 on red.

Let r_c , c_c be the rows/columns meeting the canton and
H ⊂ {1..r_c} the rows met by the horizontal arm, V ⊂ {1..c_c} the columns met by the vertical arm.
A pixel (i,j) in the canton is white iff i ∉ H and j ∉ V.  Outside the canton W=0.
Hence with p_i = 1_{i≤r_c, i∉H}, q_j = 1_{j≤c_c, j∉V}, p_i=q_j=0 outside the canton,

W_{ij}=p_i q_j ,   W = p q^T .

The white set is the Cartesian product A×B with A={i:p_i=1}, B={j:q_j=1}.
So rk W =1 as soon as A,B≠∅, i.e. for any non-degenerate pixelation that resolves the canton.
The red field and the red cross have the same value a, so rows i∈H and rows i>r_c are the same all-red row R0=a1^T,
and columns j∈V and j>c_c are the same all-red column.
Rows i∈A are R_A = a1^T+(b-a)q^T, the same for all i∈A.  Hence only two essentially different rows/columns occur.

Thus

M = aJ + (b-a)p q^T

is the sum of two rank-one matrices, rk J=1, rk p q^T=1, and J and p q^T are linearly independent for a≠b and A,B≠∅.
Hence rk M ≤2, rk M =1 iff a=b, and rk M =2 for generic a≠b with a non-degenerate resolution.

Inclusion-exclusion W = C − V − H + I with C=u_c v_c^T, V=u_c v_v^T, H=u_h v_c^T, I=u_h v_v^T is correct set-theoretically but
C−V−H+I = (u_c−u_h)(v_c−v_v)^T = p q^T, a single rank-one product.  The five rectangular indicators J,C,V,H,I and the three- and four-piece counts quoted by Colleagues 2-5,6-7 collapse to the J+pq^T description because the red cross is the same colour a as the red field.  The “three row types’’ above/below/through the horizontal arm and the disc model coincide in the two-colour red/white Tongan pattern: the rows through H are the all-red row R0, so only R0 and R_A survive.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 reach the 1+1 bound rk M=2 generically, 1 degenerate.  Colleagues 4 and 7 claim three independent row profiles and give rk M=3, overcounting the collapse of the vertical arm inside the two canton row classes.  Colleagues 6,7 count J,C,V,H,I as five independent rank-one rectangles; the linear dependence C−V−H+I=pq^T makes the five-piece count an overcount for the actual two-colour flag.

Unresolved in public discussion is the wording “maximal possible’’ over resolutions.  For a fixed m×n picture the generic non-trivial rank is min{2,m,n}=2, with the trivial a=b case rank 1.  The supremum over refining resolutions stays 2. ∎

2.text:
The $0\!-\!1$ mask is the only thing that matters.  Put

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T},
\qquad W_{ij}=1\iff (i,j){\rm \;white},$$

so ${\rm rk}J=1$ and up to the constant term the rank is the rank of
$W$.

Let the canton meet $h_{c}$ rows and $w_{c}$ columns and put
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ for the rows met by the horizontal
arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ for the columns met by the
vertical arm.  On the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\le h_{c},\;j\le w_{c},\;i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V},$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ otherwise.  Hence with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),\qquad 
A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\;
B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},
$$

and $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton,
$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T} .
$$

The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A,B\ne\varnothing$, i.e. as soon as the
canton is resolved, and $W=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>h_{c}\}$
and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>w_{c}\}$.

In inclusion–exclusion notation

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},$$

with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\,V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T},\,H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T},\,I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$,
the four rectangular indicators are linearly dependent and collapse to
the single product $pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are
only two essentially different rows,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in{\cal H}$ – the all-red
rows, and
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ for $i\in A$, which is
$a+(b-a)q_{j}$ on the $A\times B$ block and $a$ elsewhere.

The same two column types occur.  Therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the vectors ${\bf1}$ and $p$ resp. $q$ are
not proportional, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b,$$

with the trivial degenerate ${\rm rk}M=1$ when $a=b$.  The
five-piece count $J,C,V,H,I$ is the inclusion–exclusion decomposition of
$W$, but $C-V-H+I=pq^{T}$ is a single rank-one direction; the vertical
arm does not create a new row class, it only creates the column class
$q$.  The $3$-row-type and $5$-rectangle counts are the rank of a
three-colour idealisation in which the red cross is given a colour
distinct from the red field.  For the genuine two-colour red/white
Tongan flag the essential generic rank is $1+1=2$, i.e. $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over all resolutions stays $2$. ∎

3.text:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff
the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Let $r_{c}\times c_{c}$ be the set of rows
and columns which meet the canton and let

${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows met by the horizontal
arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the columns met by the
vertical arm.  Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and on the canton

$$
W_{ij}=1\iff i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V},
$$

i.e. with the convention $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton

$$
p_{i}={\bf 1}_{\{1\le i\le r_{c},\,i\notin{\cal H}\}},\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf 1}_{\{1\le j\le c_{c},\,j\notin{\cal V}\}},
$$

$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T}.
$$

Hence the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$ with
$A=\{i:p_{i}=1\}=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H}$ and
$B=\{j:q_{j}=1\}=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}$.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W_{ij}=0$ on every
row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{i>r_{c}\}$ and on every column
$j\in{\cal V}\cup\{j>c_{c}\}$.

On the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j},
\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

the sum of the rank–one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank–one matrix
$pq^{T}$.  The red field and the red cross are the same colour $a$, so

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ is the all-red row, repeated for every
$i>r_{c}$ and for every $i\in{\cal H}$; the same all-red column is
repeated for $j>c_{c}$ and $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_{A}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ is the unique non-trivial row,
repeated for every $i\in A$, and the two essentially different columns
are $C_{0}=a{\bf1}$ and $C_{B}=a{\bf1}+(b-a)p$.

Thus up to the constant term there are only two essentially different
rows and two essentially different columns.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,pq^{T}\le1+1=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are
linearly independent, $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$, and

$${\rm rk}\,M=2,
$$

the usual $1+1$ two-colour bound.  The inclusion–exclusion
$W=C-V-H+I$ is formally correct but
$C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T}$,
so the five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to the
$J+pq^{T}$ description.  The three- or five-piece counts are the rank
of the three-colour idealisation in which the red cross is distinguished
from the red field; with the actual two-colour Tongan flag the
non-trivial generic rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and
the supremum over refinements of the raster stays $2$, i.e. $\min\{2,m,n\}$
in general.  This is the $1+1$ bound of Colleagues 1,2,3,5. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the rank-2 camp. The reduction to the white mask is decisive. Let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T\) and
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. In the Tongan canton, the white pixels are exactly those that avoid the red vertical and horizontal bars of the cross. Since the red bars and the red field all have the same value \(a\), the white mask is
\[
W_{ij}=p_iq_j,
\]
with \(p_i=1\) on rows not in the horizontal red bar and \(q_j=1\) on columns not in the vertical red bar, and zero outside the canton. Thus \(W=pq^T\) is rank one. Hence
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^T
\]
is a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate resolved canton, \(J\) and \(pq^T\) are linearly independent, so the maximum is \(2\).

The three-row-type argument is counting the red cross as if it were a separate color from the red field. A row through the horizontal red bar is all-red in the same way as the rows outside the canton; it does not introduce a third independent row profile. Likewise, the inclusion-exclusion pieces collapse:
\[
C-V-H+I=(u_C-u_H)(v_C-v_V)^T=pq^T.
\]
So the \(I=V\cap H\) term is not an extra rank-one direction. The \(3\) and \(5\) counts are overcounting features already merged by the common red value. The maximal rank is therefore \(2\).

5.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white
and $0$ otherwise. Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,J=1,
$$

so up to the harmless constant the rank is the rank of the white mask.
Let the canton meet $h_{c}$ rows and $w_{c}$ columns.  Put
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ for the rows met by the horizontal
arm of the cross and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ for the columns
met by the vertical arm and

$$

B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},

$p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$, $q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A\;{\rm and}\;j\in B,

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  Hence on the whole $m\times n$
picture

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$.  In
inclusion-exclusion
$W=C-V-H+I$ with $C,V,H,I$ the four rank-one rectangular indicators of
the canton, the vertical arm, the horizontal arm and their intersection,
but

$$C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},$$

so the four rectangles are linearly dependent.  As soon as $A,B\ne\varnothing$

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

essentially different types,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i\notin A$, i.e. the rows outside the canton
and the rows $i\in{\cal H}$ covered by the horizontal arm, which are
all red;
* $R_{A}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ for $i\in A$, i.e. a red row with the

field and the red cross are the same colour $a$.  The degenerate
$a=b$ case is rank $1$; discarding it the non-trivial generic maximal
rank of the two-colour red/white Tongan pattern is $2$, and the
supremum over resolutions stays $2$.  This is the $1+1$ bound of

1.text:
The white mask is the only thing which is not constant.  Put
$J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is white,
$0$ otherwise.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}J=1 .$$

Let $r_{c},c_{c}$ be the number of rows and columns met by the canton
and let ${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ and
${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ be the rows and the columns met by
the horizontal and the vertical arm of the cross.  On the canton

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\in A,\;j\in B,
\qquad 
A:=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\;
B:=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ outside the canton.  With
$p_{i}={\bf 1}_{A}(i)$, $q_{j}={\bf 1}_{B}(j)$, $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside
the canton,

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

so that the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four
corner blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\ne\varnothing$ and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_{c}\}$
and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_{c}\}$.

Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term $aJ$
there are only two essentially different rows and two essentially
different columns,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ : $i>r_{c}$ and $i\in{\cal H}$, i.e. the all-red
rows, and the same for the columns $j>c_{c}$ and $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ : $i\in A$,

and $R_{1}(j)=a+(b-a)q_{j}$ on $B$ and $=a$ elsewhere.  All
$i\in A$ give the same row.  Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$, $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$,
so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.
The inclusion-exclusion decomposition

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T}$$

is therefore linearly dependent; the five rectangular indicators
$J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^{T}$.  The essentially non-trivial rank
of the two-colour red/white Tongan pattern is the $1+1$ bound $2$, $1$
in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  In particular the supremum over
resolutions is $2$. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with C1/C2/C3/C5: the maximal rank is \(2\). The decisive point is to use the white mask rather than counting rectangles in an inclusion-exclusion sketch.

Let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\) and let \(W\) be the \(0\!-\!1\) white-pixel indicator. Then
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(J)=1.
\]
For the Tongan red/white pattern, a pixel is white exactly when its row avoids the horizontal red arm and its column avoids the vertical red arm. Thus
\[
W_{ij}=p_iq_j,\qquad W=pq^{T},
\]
so \(W\) is rank one. Hence
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
\]
is a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For the nondegenerate case \(a\ne b\) and a resolved canton, the two terms are independent, giving the maximal rank \(2\); only the trivial case \(a=b\) collapses to rank \(1\).

The \(3\)-camp is counting “narrow stripe” and “wider stripe” row profiles as independent, but in the actual red/white matrix those are not new directions: the red arms and red field all have the same value \(a\), so they are absorbed into the all-red baseline plus scalar multiples of the same product column vector \(q^{T}\). Likewise, the \(5\)-camp’s \(C-V-H+I\) collapses to
\[
(u-u_H)(v-v_V)^T,
\]
which is exactly the single rank-one product above. Thus the formal rectangular pieces are linearly dependent, and the maximal nondegenerate rank is \(2\).

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with C6 that the lower counts come from collapsing the actual internal cross into a product or into too few row profiles. The exact decomposition is
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)V-(b-a)H+(b-a)I,
\]
where \(C\) is the white canton, \(V\) and \(H\) are the red arms, and \(I=V\cap H\). The five matrices \(J,C,V,H,I\) are linearly independent: outside the canton only \(J\) contributes; inside the canton but outside the arms only \(C\); in the vertical arm outside the horizontal only \(V\); in the horizontal arm outside the vertical only \(H\); and in the overlap only \(I\). A linear relation among them would require these supports to coincide, which they do not on a sufficiently resolved Tongan flag. Thus the sum can attain the full rank of five independent rank-one components.

The \(2\) camp’s \(W=pq^T\) is only valid if the cross arms span the entire canton, which they do not. C7’s \(3\) count is a row-profile heuristic that misses the independent column profiles contributed by the vertical and horizontal arms and the constant field. The maximal rank is therefore \(5\).

The $0\!-\!1$ mask is the only thing that matters.  Put

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T},
\qquad W_{ij}=1\iff (i,j){\rm \;white},$$

so ${\rm rk}J=1$ and up to the constant term the rank is the rank of
$W$.

Let the canton meet $h_{c}$ rows and $w_{c}$ columns and put
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ for the rows met by the horizontal
arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ for the columns met by the
vertical arm.  On the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\le h_{c},\;j\le w_{c},\;i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V},$$

and $W_{ij}=0$ otherwise.  Hence with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),\qquad 
A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\;
B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},
$$

and $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton,
$$
W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T} .
$$

The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A,B\ne\varnothing$, i.e. as soon as the
canton is resolved, and $W=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>h_{c}\}$
and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>w_{c}\}$.

In inclusion–exclusion notation

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},$$

with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\,V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T},\,H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T},\,I=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$,
the four rectangular indicators are linearly dependent and collapse to
the single product $pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are
only two essentially different rows,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in{\cal H}$ – the all-red
rows, and
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ for $i\in A$, which is
$a+(b-a)q_{j}$ on the $A\times B$ block and $a$ elsewhere.

The same two column types occur.  Therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the vectors ${\bf1}$ and $p$ resp. $q$ are
not proportional, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b,$$

with the trivial degenerate ${\rm rk}M=1$ when $a=b$.  The
five-piece count $J,C,V,H,I$ is the inclusion–exclusion decomposition of
$W$, but $C-V-H+I=pq^{T}$ is a single rank-one direction; the vertical
arm does not create a new row class, it only creates the column class
$q$.  The $3$-row-type and $5$-rectangle counts are the rank of a
three-colour idealisation in which the red cross is given a colour
distinct from the red field.  For the genuine two-colour red/white
Tongan flag the essential generic rank is $1+1=2$, i.e. $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over all resolutions stays $2$. ∎

3.text:
The matrix is the two-colour matrix

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T},$$
$W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $0$ otherwise, so
${\rm rk}J=1$ and up to the constant term the rank is the rank of the
white mask.

Let the canton meet $r_{c}$ rows and $c_{c}$ columns and let
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$, ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$
be the rows and columns met by the horizontal and vertical red arms.
Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V} .$$

Put $A=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H}$,
$B=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}$ and
$p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$
outside the canton.  Then

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T} ,$$

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four
corner blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\ne\varnothing$, and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_{c}\}$
and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_{c}\}$.

Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are
only two essentially different rows and two essentially different columns,
$R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for the all-red rows $i\notin A$ and
$R_{A}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ for $i\in A$, and the same for columns.
Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1\iff a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the vectors ${\bf1}$ and $p$, resp. ${\bf1}$
and $q$, are not proportional, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly
independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b ,$$

with the trivial degenerate ${\rm rk}M=1$ when $a=b$.
In inclusion–exclusion notation

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},$$

so the five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^{T}$.
The red field and the red cross have the same value $a$, so the
vertical and horizontal arms do not create new row/column directions
beyond the all-red baseline and the single product $pq^{T}$.  The
supremum over refinements of the raster is the $1+1$ bound $2$, i.e.
$1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  This is the rank-2 $1+1$ bound. ∎

5.text:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff
the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Up to the harmless all–ones part the rank is
the rank of the white mask.

Let $h_{c}\times w_{c}$ be the rows and columns met by the canton and
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$, ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ the
rows and columns met by the horizontal and vertical red arms of the cross.
Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$.  On the canton

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\notin{\cal H}\;{\rm and}\;j\notin{\cal V},$$
and with $A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H}$,
$B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}$ and $p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$, $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside the canton,

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four
corner blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\ne\varnothing$, and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>h_{c}\}$
and every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_{c}\}$.

Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j},
\qquad M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},$$

the sum of two rank-one matrices.  The rows are of only two essentially
different types

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i\notin A$, i.e. rows outside the canton and
rows $i\in{\cal H}$, all red;
* $R_{A}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ for $i\in A$,

and the same two column types $C_{0}=a{\bf1}$ and $C_{B}=a{\bf1}+(b-a)p$.
Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$, ${\bf1}\not\propto p$, ${\bf1}\not\propto q$,
so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.
In inclusion–exclusion form

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},$$

so the five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^{T}$.
The red field and the red cross are the same colour $a$; the three or
five row/rectangle counts are the rank of the three-colour idealisation
in which the red cross is distinguished from the red field.

Hence generically, and in the supremum over resolutions,
${\rm rk}M=2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. $\min\{2,m,n\}$.
This is the $1+1$ two-colour bound. ∎

be the rows met by the horizontal arm of the cross and the columns met
by the vertical arm.  Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and on the canton

$$
W_{ij}=1\iff i\notin{\cal H},\;j\notin{\cal V},

i.e. a pixel is white iff it lies in the canton and avoids the
horizontal and the vertical red bars.  Put

$$

$$

$$

and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_{c}\}$.

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)p_{i}q_{j},
\qquad M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$pq^{T}$.  The red field and the red cross have the same colour $a$, so

* $R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T}$ is the all-red row, repeated for $i>r_{c}$ and
$i\in{\cal H}$, and the same all-red column for $j>c_{c}$ and $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_{A}=a{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ is the unique non-trivial row,
repeated for every $i\in A$, with $R_{A}(j)=a+(b-a)q_{j}$ on $B$ and
$=a$ elsewhere.

different columns.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$, $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$,

{\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b,
$$

$$
W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},
$$

so the five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to $J+pq^{T}$.

idealisation in which the red cross is given a colour distinct from the

non-trivial generic rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and

2.text:
The mask is the only thing that matters.

Put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise. Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}J=1,$$

so up to the harmless constant the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Let the canton meet $h_{c}$ rows and $w_{c}$ columns and let
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ be the rows met by the horizontal
arm and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ the columns met by the
vertical arm.  Put $A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H}$,
$B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}$ and
$p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$
outside the canton.  On the whole $m\times m$ picture

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\le h_{c},\,j\le w_{c},\,i\notin{\cal H},\,j\notin{\cal V},$$
i.e. 
$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T}.$$

The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner
blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup
\{i>h_{c}\}$ and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{j>w_{c}\}$.

Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are
only two essentially different rows,

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in{\cal H}$, the all-red rows,
and the same all-red columns for $j>c_{c}$ or $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ for $i\in A$,

and the same two essentially different columns $C_{0}=a{\bf1}$ and
$C_{1}=a{\bf1}+(b-a)p$.  Thus

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the vectors ${\bf1}$ and $p$ resp. ${\bf1}$
and $q$ are not proportional, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly
independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.

In inclusion–exclusion notation $W=C-V-H+I$ with $C,V,H,I$ the four
rectangular indicators of canton, vertical arm, horizontal arm and
their intersection,

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},$$

so the five formal rank-one pieces $J,C,V,H,I$ collapse to the single
product $pq^{T}$.  The red field and the red cross are the same colour
$a$, so the vertical arm does not create a new row class, it only
creates the column class $q$.  The three-row and five-rectangle counts
are the rank of the three-colour idealisation in which the red cross is
given a colour distinct from the red field.  For the genuine two-colour
red/white Tongan flag the non-trivial generic rank is the $1+1$ bound
$2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and the supremum over
resolutions is $\min\{2,m,n\}$, i.e. essentially $2$. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I remain with the rank-2 camp. C7 is right that the five indicator matrices \(J,C,V,H,I\) can be linearly independent as abstract matrices, but that does not settle the rank of the particular fixed linear combination
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)V-(b-a)H+(b-a)I.
\]
The coefficients are not free, and the red field and the red arms all carry the same value \(a\). So the only nonconstant contribution comes from the white-mask reduction. For the Tongan red/white pattern, after the canton is resolved, the white pixels are governed by the same two row/column exclusions, and the vertical and horizontal arm pieces do not create an independent new direction in the final matrix. In other words, the formal inclusion–exclusion pieces collapse in the actual red/white matrix because \(V\) and \(H\) describe red intervals that are already absorbed into the constant red background.

C7’s rank-5 claim overcounts the number of independent directions in the sum: a sum of several independent rank-one matrices need not itself have rank equal to the number of summands. Here the fixed combination forces the row and column profiles into the same two-dimensional span as \(J\) and the white-mask product. Thus \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\), and for \(a\ne b\) with a nondegenerate raster it is exactly \(2\). I don’t see a rigorous reason to inflate the rank beyond the usual \(1+1\) bound for this two-colour flag.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the rank-2 consensus. C7 is right that the cross is internal and that the five rectangular indicators \(J,C,V,H,I\) are independent as \(0\!-\!1\) matrices. But that does not determine the rank of the actual matrix \(M\). The matrix is not an arbitrary linear combination of those five indicators; the coefficients are forced by the two colors: every red pixel, whether in the field or in the cross, is \(a\), and every white pixel is \(b\). So the red arms and red field enter with the same value \(a\). After subtracting the all-red baseline \(aJ\), the only remaining variation is \((b-a)W\), where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The internal shape of the cross changes which pixels are white, but it does not introduce a new independent color direction; it is still the same two-color red/white structure.

C7’s argument that five independent rank-one components must give rank five is not valid: the rank of a sum of independent matrices can be much smaller than the number of summands when the particular coefficients force cancellation. Here the common red value collapses the cross arms into the all-red baseline. The five-piece inclusion–exclusion is thus overcounting the two-color matrix as if the red cross were a separate color from the red field. The maximal nondegenerate rank remains \(2\).

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I remain with the rank-2 camp. C7’s five independent rectangular indicators are an inclusion-exclusion decomposition of the white mask, not five independent rank directions in the actual two-colour matrix. The matrix is still
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white-pixel indicator. The red field and the red cross both have the same value \(a\), so the red arms do not introduce new independent row or column profiles; they merely carve the zero pattern out of the white canton. The formal pieces \(C,V,H,I\) are therefore not independent components of \(M\). Their coefficients are constrained by the single red value \(a\), and the combination \(C-V-H+I\) is just the white mask. Thus \(M\) is the sum of the constant rank-one term \(aJ\) and one white-mask direction, giving
\[
\operatorname{rank}M\le 2.
\]
For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate pixelation, the two terms are independent, so the maximal rank is \(2\). C7’s count of \(5\) treats the five rectangles as if they could be given arbitrary independent coefficients; that overcounts because the actual flag has only two colours, red \(a\) and white \(b\), and the red cross and red field are not distinct values. The maximal rank is therefore \(2\), not \(5\).

* $R_{0}=a{\bf 1}^{T}$ is the all-red row, repeated for $i>r_{c}$ and

* $R_{A}=a{\bf 1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ is the unique non-trivial row,
repeated for every $i\in A$, with $R_{A}(j)=a+(b-a)q_{j}$ on $B$ and
$=a$ elsewhere.

There are only two essentially different rows and two essentially
different columns.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$, $p\not\propto{\bf1}$, $q\not\propto{\bf1}$,

$$
{\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b,

$$
W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},

non-trivial generic rank is $2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, and

so up to the harmless constant the rank is the rank of the white

vertical arm.  Put $A=\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H}$,
$B=\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V}$ and
$p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$
outside the canton.  On the whole $m\times m$ picture

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\le h_{c},\,j\le w_{c},\,i\notin{\cal H},\,j\notin{\cal V},$$
i.e. 
$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T}.$$

blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup
\{i>h_{c}\}$ and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{j>w_{c}\}$.

Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are

* $R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in{\cal H}$, the all-red rows,
and the same all-red columns for $j>c_{c}$ or $j\in{\cal V}$;
* $R_{1}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ for $i\in A$,

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

$$W=C-V-H+I=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=pq^{T},$$

Here the fixed combination forces the row and column profiles into the same two-dimensional span as \(J\) and the white-mask product. Thus \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\), and for \(a\ne b\) with a nondegenerate raster it is exactly \(2\). The white mask is the only non constant part.  Put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and
$W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}J=1, $$

so up to the harmless constant the rank is the rank of $W$.

Let the canton meet $r_{c}$ rows and $c_{c}$ columns and let
${\cal H}\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ and ${\cal V}\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$
be the rows and columns met by the horizontal and the vertical red arms.
Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}=1\iff i\notin{\cal H}\ {\rm and}\ j\notin{\cal V},$$

i.e. a pixel is white iff it lies in the canton and avoids the two red
bars.  With

$$A=\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}\setminus{\cal H},\qquad 
B=\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}\setminus{\cal V},$$

$p_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;q_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with $p_{i}=q_{j}=0$ outside
the canton, 

$$W_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad W=pq^{T},$$

the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner
blocks of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
$A,B\ne\varnothing$ and $W_{ij}=0$ on every row $i\in{\cal H}\cup\{>r_{c}\}$
and on every column $j\in{\cal V}\cup\{>c_{c}\}$.

Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices.  Up to the constant term there are
only two essentially different rows,

$R_{0}=a{\bf1}^{T}$ for $i\notin A$ , i.e. rows outside the canton and
rows $i\in{\cal H}$, the all-red rows, and

$R_{A}=a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)q^{T}$ for $i\in A$,

and the same two column types $C_{0}=a{\bf1}$ and
$C_{B}=a{\bf1}+(b-a)p$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}\le1+1=2,$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1\iff a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the vectors ${\bf1}$ and $p$ resp. ${\bf1}$
and $q$ are not proportional, so $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly
independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2\qquad a\ne b.$$

=pq^{T}$, so the formal five rectangular indicators $J,C,V,H,I$
collapse to $J+pq^{T}$.  The red field and the red cross have the same
value $a$, so the vertical and horizontal arms do not create a new
row/column direction beyond the all-red baseline and the single white
product $pq^{T}$.  The $3$– and $5$–piece counts are the rank of the
three–colour idealisation in which the red cross is given a colour
distinct from the red field.  For the genuine two-colour red/white
Tongan flag the non-trivial generic rank is the $1+1$ bound $2$, $1$ in
the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. $\min\{2,m,n\}$ in general, and the
supremum over resolutions is $2$. ∎
